# Generated eve project

**Do not edit anything in here.** Every file is generated by ai-team from the `team` and
`agent` rows in its database (D2), and the next regeneration overwrites it.

To change what these agents are, change the team:

```sh
ait agents generate --project <slug>   # rewrite this directory from the rows
```

## What is here

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `agent/agent.ts` | the orchestrator - the root agent |
| `agent/subagents/<role>/` | one declared subagent per seat on the team |
| `agent/lib/worktree.ts` | the single seam deciding what "inside the worktree" means |
| `agent/lib/tools.ts` | the authored tool implementations |
| `agent/tools/` | the tool slots eve discovers, re-exporting from `lib/` |

`agent/tools/bash.ts`, `read_file.ts` and `write_file.ts` deliberately occupy the same
slots as eve's sandbox defaults, replacing them. Agents edit the worktree ai-team leased
for them, not eve's sandbox (D3).

The worktree is `$AI_TEAM_WORKTREE`, set by ai-team on this process. One eve process is
started per leased worktree (D10), so isolation is an OS fact rather than a check.

There is no `agent/connections/` directory, deliberately. eve's MCP connections are
HTTP-only, and ai-planner and file-sql both speak MCP over stdio - so they are reached
another way, wired up in M2-S8.
